# Setup questions, explained

<!-- Generated by `python3 -m lifekit guide`; edit lifekit/questions.py instead. -->

`life-kit setup` asks these in order and saves each answer as you go, so you can stop
and resume. At any prompt type `skip` to leave it unknown, or `back` to redo the previous
answer. Nothing is sent anywhere while you answer: answers stay in your workspace under
`.local/setup-answers.json`. Secrets (tokens, keys) are typed hidden and stored separately.

## Basics

Who you are and where your workspace lives. Two minutes.

### Which currency do you use? (3-letter code)

- **Why:** Money is stored exactly in one currency; amounts in different currencies are never added together.
- **Example:** INR, USD, EUR, GBP
- **If you skip:** Cannot be skipped: the workspace needs it.

### What should assistants call you?

- **Why:** Skills and reports address you by this name instead of 'the user'.
- **Example:** Priya
- **If you skip:** Assistants will say 'you'.

### What is your timezone?

- **Why:** Dates like 'today' and 'this week' depend on it. Schedules use your computer's clock.
- **Example:** Asia/Kolkata, Europe/London, America/New_York
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.

## Life areas

Pick the parts of life you want help with. You can add more later by re-running setup.

### Which life areas do you want? (comma-separated numbers or names)

- **Why:** Each area gets its own folder, skills and optional scheduled runs. Unpicked areas stay out of the way.
- **Example:** personal, finance, career
- **If you skip:** Only the core check-in, spending and review commands are set up.
- **Choices:** personal, finance, career, work

## Rules and routine

Your boundaries and rhythm. Every assistant reads these before doing anything.

### When are you usually busy with work or study?

- **Why:** Assistants avoid suggesting tasks in these hours.
- **Example:** Mon-Fri 10:00-19:00
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.

### When do you realistically have free time on a normal day?

- **Why:** Plans that ignore your real time get abandoned. Suggestions fit inside this.
- **Example:** 45 minutes after dinner, more on Sundays
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.

### What time suits a short daily review? (HH:MM, 24-hour)

- **Why:** The nightly report runner defaults to this time.
- **Example:** 22:00
- **If you skip:** The nightly report suggests 22:00; you can change it later.

### Anything that must never leave this computer or be shared?

- **Why:** Written into your rules. Personal and money files stay local by default either way.
- **Example:** Never mention my health to anyone; never upload bank statements
- **If you skip:** The default applies: personal and finance stay local.

### How should assistants talk to you?

- **Why:** Sets the voice of reports and coaching.
- **Example:** Direct and short. Push me when I slack.
- **If you skip:** A neutral, concise tone.

## Personal context

A short portrait so suggestions fit your real life.

### What personal goals matter this year?

- **Why:** Daily suggestions are checked against these.
- **Example:** Gym 4x/week, sleep 7h, call parents on Sundays
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** personal area enabled

### Describe a normal day in one or two lines.

- **Why:** Helps assistants place reminders and prep at times that actually work.
- **Example:** Wake 8, office 10-7, gym 8pm, dinner 9:30
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** personal area enabled

### Anything else an assistant should always remember about you?

- **Why:** Pinned in your personal context file, verbatim.
- **Example:** I'm vegetarian; I prefer mornings for deep work
- **If you skip:** Nothing pinned.
- **Asked when:** personal area enabled

## Money

Numbers are stored with today's date, so nobody mistakes an old number for a current one.

### Monthly take-home income? (number in your currency)

- **Why:** Used for budgets and 'can I afford this' answers, dated today.
- **Example:** 90000
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** finance area enabled

### Roughly what do you spend in a month? (number)

- **Why:** A baseline to compare actual spending against. Your own estimate, labelled as such.
- **Example:** 40000
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** finance area enabled

### What are your money goals?

- **Why:** The finance skill prioritises advice against these.
- **Example:** 6-month emergency fund, then index funds monthly
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** finance area enabled

### Will you drop bank statement CSV files into finance/inbox/?

- **Why:** Then spending is imported and posted automatically each night, using category rules you approve.
- **Example:** yes
- **If you skip:** No automatic import; log spending by hand or by phone.
- **Asked when:** finance area enabled

## Career

Your current job, where you want to go, and how you prepare.

### What is your current role and experience?

- **Why:** Job search and prep skills tailor to your level.
- **Example:** Backend engineer, 2 years, Node + Postgres
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** career area enabled

### What role and pay are you aiming for, and by when?

- **Why:** Job discovery filters by this; prep plans work back from the date.
- **Example:** SDE-2 backend, 30L+, within 6 months
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** career area enabled

### Where can you work?

- **Why:** Filters job listings.
- **Example:** Bangalore or remote (India)
- **If you skip:** All locations considered.
- **Asked when:** career area enabled

### Path to your current resume file (PDF or source)?

- **Why:** Applications record a fingerprint of the exact file used. The file is never uploaded by setup.
- **Example:** ~/Documents/resume.pdf
- **If you skip:** Resume-related steps will ask for it when needed.
- **Asked when:** career area enabled

### Which interview topics do you want to practise?

- **Why:** The prep skill builds a plan from these.
- **Example:** DSA, system design, SQL, behavioural
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** career area enabled

## Day job

Context for standups, tickets and work briefs.

### Where do you work, and what is your role?

- **Why:** Standups and work briefs use it. Stays in your private workspace.
- **Example:** Acme Corp, backend engineer
- **If you skip:** Recorded as unknown. Assistants will ask instead of guessing.
- **Asked when:** work area enabled

### Which work tools do you use? (comma-separated)

- **Why:** Suggests matching connections later.
- **Example:** github, slack, clickup
- **If you skip:** No work tools suggested.
- **Choices:** github, gitlab, slack, clickup, jira, linear, notion, signoz, other
- **Asked when:** work area enabled

### When is your standup? (HH:MM)

- **Why:** The work brief runner is suggested 30 minutes before it.
- **Example:** 10:30
- **If you skip:** The work brief suggests 08:30.
- **Asked when:** work area enabled

## AI assistants

Which assistant apps should read this workspace. Both can share the same skills.

### Which assistants do you use? (claude, codex, or both)

- **Why:** Setup writes skills and connection config in each assistant's own format.
- **Example:** claude,codex
- **If you skip:** Skills are written but no assistant config is created.
- **Choices:** claude, codex

### Which assistant should scheduled runs use by default?

- **Why:** Each scheduled run needs one assistant to run without you. You can override per run.
- **Example:** claude
- **If you skip:** The first one you picked.
- **Choices:** claude, codex
- **Asked when:** both assistants picked

## Claude Code plugins

Optional add-ons for Claude Code. Pick what you like; none are required.

### Which Claude Code plugins should be installed? (comma-separated, or none)

- **Why:** Plugins add workflows to Claude Code. superpowers: Structured brainstorming, planning, TDD and debugging workflows. context7: Fetches current library documentation instead of guessing APIs. github: GitHub integration for PRs and issues from Claude Code. code-review: Reviews diffs and pull requests for bugs. skill-creator: Create and improve your own skills, like the ones in this workspace. frontend-design: Better visual design when building pages or dashboards.
- **Example:** superpowers, context7
- **If you skip:** No plugins installed; you can install any later with `claude plugin install`.
- **Choices:** superpowers, context7, github, code-review, skill-creator, frontend-design
- **Asked when:** Claude Code picked

### Run the plugin install commands now?

- **Why:** Installs into your Claude Code user settings (not this workspace). Say no to just see the commands.
- **Example:** yes
- **If you skip:** Commands are printed for you to run later.
- **Asked when:** any plugin picked

## Connections

Optional accounts your assistant may read: mail, calendar, work tools, broker, shopping.

### Which connections do you want? (comma-separated, or none)

- **Why:** Each lets your assistant READ one service. Writes like sending, ordering or editing tickets stay off. gmail = Gmail; google-calendar = Google Calendar; google-drive = Google Drive; slack = Slack; github = GitHub; clickup = ClickUp; notion = Notion; linear = Linear; signoz = SigNoz; kite = Zerodha Kite (read-only); zepto = Zepto; swiggy-instamart = Swiggy Instamart; swiggy-food = Swiggy Food; zomato = Zomato; linkedin = LinkedIn (community server);
- **Example:** gmail, google-calendar, github
- **If you skip:** No connections. Everything works from local files.
- **Choices:** gmail, google-calendar, google-drive, slack, github, clickup, notion, linear, signoz, kite, zepto, swiggy-instamart, swiggy-food, zomato, linkedin

### GitHub: GitHub token (read-only)

- **Why:** Stored only in your workspace's .local/secrets.json and passed to assistants as LIFEKIT_GITHUB_TOKEN. Create a fine-grained personal access token at https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens with read-only access to the repositories you want. Paste it at the hidden prompt. Alternatively keep using the `gh` CLI (`gh auth login`).
- **Example:** (typed hidden)
- **If you skip:** GitHub is configured but cannot log in until you add it with `life-kit connect add github`.
- **Asked when:** github picked
- **Typed hidden** and stored only in your workspace, never in answers or logs.

### SigNoz: SigNoz URL (https://...)

- **Why:** Stored only in your workspace's .local/secrets.json and passed to assistants as SIGNOZ_URL. Install signoz-mcp-server (see docs) so the command is on your PATH. SigNoz Cloud users can instead add its hosted endpoint as a custom connection. Create an API key in SigNoz settings; paste your SigNoz URL and the key at the prompts.
- **Example:** (typed hidden)
- **If you skip:** SigNoz is configured but cannot log in until you add it with `life-kit connect add signoz`.
- **Asked when:** signoz picked
- **Typed hidden** and stored only in your workspace, never in answers or logs.

### SigNoz: SigNoz API key

- **Why:** Stored only in your workspace's .local/secrets.json and passed to assistants as SIGNOZ_API_KEY. Install signoz-mcp-server (see docs) so the command is on your PATH. SigNoz Cloud users can instead add its hosted endpoint as a custom connection. Create an API key in SigNoz settings; paste your SigNoz URL and the key at the prompts.
- **Example:** (typed hidden)
- **If you skip:** SigNoz is configured but cannot log in until you add it with `life-kit connect add signoz`.
- **Asked when:** signoz picked
- **Typed hidden** and stored only in your workspace, never in answers or logs.

### Check each connection now with one real read?

- **Why:** Configured is not connected. This runs your assistant once per connection with only one read tool allowed and records the result. Log in first (steps are printed after setup).
- **Example:** no (log in first, then run `life-kit connect verify ID`)
- **If you skip:** Connections stay 'configured, not verified' until you run `life-kit connect verify ID`.
- **Asked when:** any connection picked
